maya: heads up — found a keyboard/voiceover snag in the Compact insights list on the console. focus sometimes jumps past the visible row when you use down-arrow or tab through cards. repro steps below. maya: repro (short): ``` 1) Console > Insights > switch to Compact view 2) tab to the list and use Down Arrow to move through rows 3) sometimes focus lands on a non-visible item or the row is removed and focus jumps to the list root ``` maya: seems tied to virtualization + our current roving-tabindex implementation. also noticed the selected pill outline is very faint on dark theme (low contrast). asher: @maya thanks — can you paste the DOM snippet around the list? are we using role="listbox"/aria-activedescendant or plain role="list" with tabindex on items? maya: sure — simplified: ```html
...
...
``` lina: virtualized lists + roving tabindex are tricky. when DOM nodes are removed focus can be lost or jump. recommend either: - keep a single focusable container and use aria-activedescendant to point to the active row, OR - preserve offscreen DOM nodes for the currently focused item, OR - move to a focus-management layer that re-anchors focus when an item is recycled. pavan: agree with Lina. aria-activedescendant is safest for screen readers if we can keep a stable container element. downside: we need to ensure keyboard focus remains visible (scroll into view). maya: also the selected pill outline: on dark theme it uses outline-color: #cfcfcf (1px). contrast is too low against our 12% hover bg. example: selected state bg = #1f2937, outline = #cfcfcf. oliver: quick suggestion — change focus ring to 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.9) on dark mode and add a focus-visible box-shadow fallback. should be sufficient for WCAG 2.1 AA. asher: technical suggestion for the list: switch to role="listbox" on the container, keep container tabindex=0, manage aria-activedescendant to id of the active row. the virtualized renderer can assign ids to rows as they mount. that way screen readers always have a single focus target and we avoid losing keyboard focus when nodes unmount. maya: that sounds good. any concerns about automation / e2e tests? we currently simulate key events on rows directly. pavan: tests should be updated to interact with the container and assert aria-activedescendant changes. also add a small e2e that asserts focus doesn't jump when row 1 is recycled. lina: one more nit: add aria-label on the expand/collapse toggles inside rows and ensure they are reachable by tab order (not just click handlers). VoiceOver didn’t announce the toggle role on macOS. maya: noted — will open a small design task with the suggested attributes and color tokens. oliver: prototype CSS patch snippet: ```css .insights-viewport[tabindex="0"]:focus { outline: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.92); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(255,255,255,0.06); } ``` asher: implementation notes: when you switch to aria-activedescendant, remember to set role="option" on rows and keep the active row id stable while it is in view. also guard against inert attribute on recycled nodes. maya: timeline? can we slot this for 1.18 patch? feels like a regression for keyboard users. pavan: yes put it as P1 for accessibility fixes — if patch risk small, target 1.18.1. maya: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/4123 — includes steps, voiceover notes, color swatches, and a tiny demo gif. oliver: :thumbsup: staging patch would be great — @deploy-bot can you run a canary after the PR? deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for branch "fix/insights-a11y-4123" to staging in 10 minutes. maya: thanks everyone — will add aria-activedescendant mock in the PR and a11y checklist. asher: happy to review the PR and the updated e2e tests. lina: I'll QA on VoiceOver + NVDA after the patch lands. pavan: copying into release notes under "accessibility fixes". maya: that’s it for now. will follow up in the issue if anything else comes up.
